free_tier.stated: Oracle may provide selected participants with Universal Credits for use on OCI. 'The value of Universal Credits available under the Program ranges from USD 5,000 to USD 60,000.' Credits are available for twelve months from the date they are made available, and unused credits expire with no cash value.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: USD 5,000 to 60,000 of OCI at Oracle's list prices, which are low for compute, buys a substantial amount of Ampere or GPU time for a year. The 12-month clock and the PAYG conversion at the end are stated, so the chain has a visible cliff.

evidence.proved: 'The value of Universal Credits available under the Program ranges from USD 5,000 to USD 60,000', quoted
'Credits are available for a period of twelve (12) months from the date they are made available', quoted

notes: Third-party summaries publish two different ceilings, USD 100,000 from the rules and USD 60,000 from the launch announcement, and one describes a Latin America rollout tied to OPN membership. The separate Oracle for Startups offer of USD 500 in OCI credits plus a 70% discount is a different product and was not read on a vendor page.
